title: Chickpeas: protein, fiber, calories, and nutrition

seo.title: Chickpeas: protein, fiber, calories, and nutrition
seo.meta_description: Cooked chickpeas provide about 164 calories, 8.9 g protein, and 7.6 g fiber per 100 g. See what changes from dry to cooked and what a real serving provides.
seo.search_intent: Understand the nutrition of cooked chickpeas, what they provide per 100 g and per serving, and why dry and cooked chickpeas should not be compared directly.

excerpt: Cooked chickpeas are far less concentrated than dry chickpeas because they absorb water. Per 100 g cooked, they provide about 164 calories, 8.9 g protein, and 7.6 g fiber. A 200 g portion delivers close to 18 g protein and 15 g fiber.
content_html:
Chickpeas are a good example of why food-composition numbers need context. One chart may show more than 20 g of protein per 100 g while another shows about 9 g. Both can be correct: one is usually dry chickpeas and the other is cooked chickpeas that have absorbed a large amount of water.

What 100 g of cooked chickpeas provides

NutrientPer 100 g cookedPer 200 g
Calories~164 kcal~328 kcal
Protein~8.9 g~17.8 g
Carbohydrate~27 g~54 g
Fiber~7.6 g~15.2 g
Fat~2.6 g~5.2 g
Iron~2.9 mg~5.8 mg

A 200 g serving is therefore substantial rather than decorative: it can provide almost 18 g of protein and roughly 15 g of fiber before anything else is added to the meal.

They are protein-rich for a legume, but not equivalent to meat gram for gram

About 8.9 g protein per 100 g cooked is meaningful. Still, cooked chicken breast is around 30 g protein per 100 g. A 200 g portion of chickpeas gives roughly 18 g protein, while 200 g chicken breast can exceed 60 g.

That comparison does not make one food “better.” Chickpeas bring something chicken does not: fiber. The same 200 g serving can provide about 15 g fiber, while meat contains none.

Dry and cooked numbers answer different questions

Dry chickpeas can contain roughly 20–21 g protein and more than 350 calories per 100 g. Once cooked, absorbed water increases their weight and dilutes those nutrients per 100 g, bringing the numbers closer to 8.9 g protein and 164 calories.

The pot has not destroyed the protein: dry chickpeas can be around 20–21 g protein/100 g while cooked chickpeas are near 8.9 g/100 g because the cooked batch contains much more water.

Chickpeas also contribute iron and folate

Cooked chickpeas provide around 2.9 mg iron per 100 g, or about 5.8 mg in 200 g. It is nonheme iron, whose absorption is more variable than heme iron from meat and seafood. Pairing the meal with vitamin C-rich foods such as peppers, tomatoes, citrus, or kiwi can improve nonheme iron absorption.

Chickpeas also contribute folate, magnesium, phosphorus, potassium, zinc, and several B vitamins. Exact values vary with variety and preparation.

Canned chickpeas are still a nutritious legume

Canned chickpeas are already hydrated and cooked, so their composition belongs in the same general category as home-cooked chickpeas rather than dry chickpeas. Sodium is the variable most likely to stand out among brands.

If salt is added, draining and rinsing removes some of the liquid on the surface. When comparing labels, use drained weight when possible and keep the food state consistent.

Are chickpeas high in calories?

At about 164 calories per 100 g cooked, chickpeas are more energy-dense than most non-starchy vegetables but far less concentrated than nuts and seeds, which often exceed 500 calories per 100 g. A 200 g serving is about 328 calories before oil, sauces, or toppings.

Two tablespoons of oil can add around 240 calories, compared with only about 20–50 calories separating many 200 g servings of different cooked legumes.

The useful takeaway

Chickpeas combine plant protein, fiber, carbohydrate, and micronutrients in one food. For practical comparisons, use cooked chickpeas against other cooked foods. A dry-bag value of 20 g protein per 100 g should never be treated as directly comparable with 9 g per 100 g from a canned or boiled product.

faq.question: How much protein is in chickpeas?
faq.answer: Cooked chickpeas provide about 8.9 g per 100 g. A 200 g portion provides roughly 17.8 g.

faq.question: How much fiber do chickpeas have?
faq.answer: About 7.6 g per 100 g cooked, or roughly 15 g in a 200 g serving.

faq.question: Why do dry chickpeas show much higher nutrition numbers?
faq.answer: They contain much less water. Cooking adds water and spreads the same solids across a larger total weight.
